summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the Australian National University (MA, by 1980) and the University of Göttingen (PhD dissertation, by 1990), and was a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).
Junko Minamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at Otani University from circa 1967 to 1974 and held a post at Kansai University.

Junsho Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven, the University of Tokyo (PhD), and under Étienne Lamotte, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura, later holding professorships at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

Junyi Tang was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at Peking University and under Thomé H. Fang and Shili Xiong, and held posts at National Central University (circa 1944–1949) and New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (circa 1953–1978).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He held an administrative post as section chief (課長) at Otani University.
Juro Watanabe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar. Nakasone held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Justin R. Ritzinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and has held posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (attested 2012) under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justus Olshausen was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Louis-Mathieu Langlès, and Jean-Daniel Kieffer, later holding posts at Kiel and the University of Königsberg.

János Szerb was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University, he held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (circa 1985–1988).
Jérôme Ducor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May from circa 1978 to 1985 and held a post at the University of Lausanne around 1995.

Józef Kowalewski was a scholar of Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Vilnius and Kazan Imperial University, he held posts at Kazan Imperial University (serving as rector in 1855) and the University of Warsaw.
József Budenz was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey from circa 1855 to 1858. He later held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1872 to 1892.

Jörg Heimbel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Tibet University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg. Heimbel held a post at the University of Hamburg as a Tibetan language lecturer (attested 2019).
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held professorships at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and served as an associate professor there from circa 2005 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg and studied under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 2000–2006) and the University of Marburg (from circa 2007).
Jürgen Neuß is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed a PhD at the Free University of Berlin by 2007.
